body:
Jeju-based resort and golf course operator The Sienna Group is moving to acquire Golfzon County, South Korea's largest golf course operator. The move follows the company's back-to-back acquisitions of two golf courses in the Seoul metropolitan area last year, reflecting a strategic push to build a nationwide golf course network. For seller MBK Partners, the deal could open the door to recovering an investment that has been delayed for years.

According to investment banking (IB) industry sources on the 6th, The Sienna Group recently finalized an internal decision to acquire Golfzon County and has begun negotiations with MBK Partners and other sellers. MBK Partners selected Morgan Stanley and Samjong KPMG as lead managers for the sale in March and has been reaching out to potential buyers.

The transaction targets the 58.37% controlling stake in Golfzon County that MBK Partners holds through a special purpose vehicle, a figure that includes convertible preferred shares. MBK Partners is reported to have secured tag-along rights over the stake held by second-largest shareholder Golfzon Holdings, which would allow for a full sale of all shares. The seller is known to be seeking a valuation of approximately 2 trillion won (approximately $1.5 billion) on a 100% equity basis.

Golfzon County was established in 2018 through a spin-off from Golfzon County Asset Management. It subsequently acquired Lake Hills Suncheon, Birdwood CC, and Eaglemont CC in succession, growing into South Korea's largest golf course operator. It currently operates 21 golf courses, of which 11 are directly owned.

MBK Partners participated as a financial investor at Golfzon County's inception, investing 114 billion won (approximately $84.9 million). It later injected an additional 290 billion won (approximately $216 million) to drive expansion. As a result, Golfzon County's consolidated revenue grew more than fourfold from 67.4 billion won (approximately $50.2 million) in 2018 to 285.2 billion won (approximately $212.4 million) last year.

The Sienna Group appears to have decided on the acquisition after highly valuing Golfzon County's nationwide golf course network and operational know-how. The company, which focuses on real estate development and resort operations, entered the golf course business in 2022 by acquiring Jeju CC, the first golf course on Jeju Island. Creating synergy by combining resorts and golf courses is its core strategy.

That strategy has been taking concrete shape since last year. After acquiring Jungbu CC in Gwangju, Gyeonggi Province, and Seragio GC in Yeoju, The Sienna Group launched products linking resort memberships with golf course benefits. Under the arrangement, purchasing a resort membership worth 1.2 billion won (approximately $890,000) entitles the buyer to use Seragio GC (now The Sienna Beluto CC) at member rates.

The company expects that acquiring Golfzon County will allow it to expand its golf course operations across the country in one stroke. It believes that golf course expansion will translate into expanded member benefits and greater competitiveness in attracting new members. In fact, it sold a limited number of memberships that include access to Jungbu CC (now The Sienna Seoul CC) at prices exceeding 2 billion won (approximately $1.5 million).

This acquisition push is also significant for MBK Partners. After Golfzon County's initial public offering (IPO) fell through in 2022, MBK Partners shifted to a sale strategy but failed to close a deal due to differences in price expectations. Last year, it lowered its asking price to the mid-1 trillion won range but still could not find a buyer.

This year's renewed sale attempt has also been bumpy. More than 20 institutions signed non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) and received investment memoranda (IMs), but only three to four submitted letters of intent (LOIs) in the preliminary bidding round. Concerns about a failed sale resurfaced when Macquarie Asset Management, which had been mentioned as a strong candidate, did not participate.

Golfzon County's growth metrics underpin the price the seller is seeking.

Note: Golfzon County was established through a spin-off in 2018. MBK Partners participated as a financial investor, investing a total of 404 billion won (approximately $300.9 million).

Remaining Challenges: Price and Financing

The key to closing the deal will be price negotiations and The Sienna Group's financing capacity. With the seller seeking 2 trillion won (approximately $1.5 billion) on a 100% equity basis, acquiring just MBK Partners' stake would require more than 1 trillion won (approximately $744.7 million). Industry observers believe that given The Sienna Group's size, attracting financial investors or securing large-scale acquisition financing will be unavoidable.

An IB industry source said, "The Sienna Group became a major player in the golf course M&A market after acquiring golf courses in succession last year," but added, "In terms of deal size, this is on a completely different level from the Jungbu CC and Seragio GC acquisitions, so there is keen interest in how The Sienna Group will raise up to 2 trillion won."

If The Sienna Group succeeds in this acquisition, the landscape of South Korea's golf course operation market is expected to shift significantly. Combining Golfzon County's 21 golf courses with those already held by The Sienna Group would create the largest golf course portfolio in South Korea under a single operator. Attention is also focused on how the membership model combining resorts and golf courses will be received in the market.
